# Jubilees Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Noah's Vineyard; Canaan's Sin; Curses and Blessings; Dividing the Earth

---

**7:1** In the seventh year of that week, Noah planted a vineyard on Mount Lubar — the Ararat mountain where the ark had landed. In the fourth year it bore fruit. He tended it carefully and brought in the harvest in the seventh month of that year.

**7:2** He pressed wine from it and stored it in a vessel, letting it age until the fifth year, until the first day of the first month.

**7:3** On that day Noah held a celebration — he and his sons gathered before him — and he drank the wine.

**7:4** While Noah was celebrating with joy, his grandson Canaan saw that he was drunk. Canaan came over, grabbed him, mocked him, and left him lying there exposed — he didn't cover him, just walked away.

**7:5** Ham, Canaan's father, saw Noah's nakedness and went outside to tell his two brothers.

**7:6** Shem and Japheth took a robe between them, walked backward into the tent, and draped it over their father. They kept their faces turned away the whole time and never looked at him.

**7:7** Noah woke up and found out everything his youngest grandson had done to him. He cursed him: "Cursed be Canaan — he will be a slave, the lowest of slaves, to his brothers."

**7:8** He blessed Shem: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem. And Canaan will be his slave."

**7:9** "May God give wide territory to Japheth, and may God live in Shem's tents. And Canaan will be their slave."

**7:10** When Ham found out that his father had cursed his son Canaan, he was deeply upset.

**7:11** Noah died and was buried on Mount Lubar in the land of Ararat.

**7:12** He had lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood, for a total of nine hundred and fifty years.

**7:13** In all the earth, only Enoch surpassed Noah in righteousness. Enoch's calling was different — he was appointed as the cosmic witness, the one who would document the deeds of every generation from creation to the final judgment.

**7:14** In the twenty-ninth jubilee, first week, Arpachshad married a woman named Rasu'eja, daughter of Susan daughter of Elam. In the third year she gave birth to Kainam.

**7:15** Kainam grew up and his father taught him to write. He went out exploring, looking for a place to settle and build a city.

**7:16** He found an inscription carved into rock by people from before the flood. He read it, copied it down — and it corrupted him. The inscription contained the Watchers' teachings about reading astronomical omens: how to predict things from the movements of the sun, moon, and stars.

**7:17** He kept it secret. He was afraid that if he told Noah, Noah would be furious with him.

**7:18** In the thirtieth jubilee, second week, first year, he married Melka, daughter of Madai son of Japheth. In the fourth year she gave him a son he named Shelah, saying: "Truly I have been sent."

**7:19** In the thirty-first jubilee, first week, second year, Shelah married Mu'ak, daughter of his father's brother Kesed.

**7:20** She bore him Eber. Eber later married 'Azurad, daughter of Nebrod, in the thirty-second jubilee, seventh week, third year.

**7:21** In the first year of the thirty-third jubilee, she gave birth to a son named Peleg — because in the days of his birth, Noah's descendants began to divide up the earth. That's why he was called Peleg.

**7:22** They divided the land quietly among themselves and then informed Noah.

**7:23** At the start of the thirty-third jubilee, the earth was formally divided into three portions — for Shem, Ham, and Japheth — each according to their inheritance, in the first year of the first week. One of the angels was sent to guide the process.

**7:24** Noah called his sons and grandsons together and presided over the lot-drawing. They stepped forward and drew their lots from Noah's chest — literally from the fold of his garment.

**7:25** Shem's lot fell on the middle region of the earth, to be his family's eternal inheritance — stretching from the middle of the Rafa mountain range, from the headwaters of the Tina River, running westward through that river until it reached the waters of the abyss where the Tina flows out and empties into the Maat Sea, which itself flows into the great ocean.

**7:26** Everything to the north went to Japheth. Everything to the south was Shem's.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The critical Jubilees variation — Canaan (not Ham) directly commits the sin (v.4) — rendered clearly. Kainam's discovery of Watcher-inscriptions (v.16) explains how forbidden astronomical knowledge survived the flood. "From the fold of his garment" (v.24) renders the Ge'ez "bosom" idiom naturally.*
